Now I'm asking the witness about his experience and now in this round of questions we will hear what he knows about it and then we will show documents from other municipalities. The supposition here was that he had direct knowledge; and I wanted to obtain from him the information whether he had any knowledge about other municipalities so I can move on to other municipalities. It appears to me to be quite fair towards the witness. I don't want to show him documents if he tells me that he was not aware of what was going on in other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Of course. Perhaps it would be clean to separate Livno and others because your question was, in a way, general, covering everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will comply with your instruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will first ask the following question. So is it obvious from those documents that pertain to the municipality of Livno that this was systematic, not just at the beginning but throughout the end of 1993, that there was this interference? I'm not saying that this was done with any bad intentions; it was done in order to defend the area. But it was interference in the -- in what was actually in the power of the HVO and the defence department.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer? Yes, well, I know that Livno as a municipality was not an exception when it came to those violations of the laws of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna by way of enacting some legislation by the municipal HVO which in various ways and in contravention of those laws of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna these matters were regulated. So this was not just a whim on the part of those people or their desire to counter the efforts of the HVO and other institutions of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, no, quite the contrary. The municipal HVOs faced enormous pressure. You have to look at things in the context of the time up to 2000 -- or 2000 of armed people right there in the middle of the municipality, lots of unemployed. Financial transactions were impossible, no money was coming in, no schools, normal life was disrupted completely, the life that people were used to. And given those pressures, the municipal authorities were often aware of the fact that they were violating the decisions of the HVO, but still they went on to pass the decisions, to enact the decisions, that they thought would be most useful to the people who actually lived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me now show you documents that we have as a follow-up to your answer to see whether this is confirmed. Could you please look at the next document, that's 2D 00535, that's the municipality of Tomislavgrad; we will now skip it because it's an exhibit, so to speed things up. The next document, which again has to do with the municipality of Posusje, we will skip it because it's an exhibit. Could we look at this document, 2D 00537, it's a decision on mandatory financing of the defence effort in -- of the Municipal Assembly of Posusje dated the 2nd of May, 1992, is this what you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the form in which this was drafted by the War Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can skip the next document because it's an exhibit and let us look at 2D 00540, it's a decision on financing the requirements of the All People's Defence issued by the Municipal Assembly of Tomislavgrad on the 20th of August, 1992. Does this decision confirm what you were telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And finally, as part of this topic, document 2D 00541. It's a document from the Tomislavgrad municipality. It's a decision on the amendments on the decision on financing of the All People's Defence. Can you confirm for me that this is yet another decision which shows how certain municipal HVOs were operating, what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what we were talking about. This was the war tax that was imposed by some municipalities on its residents or citizens living there in order to assist the financing of the defence and of course it is in contravention of the decisions and the decrees of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which defined the fiscal policy. Let me remind you that legislation was in place in HZ HB regulating this area of financial transactions and so on. So these decisions were not -- did not stem from the valid legislation of HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, we've seen several decisions dealing with how specific formations operating in the territory of those municipalities were financed. Does it mean that the formations that operated in municipalities were actually financed by the municipalities themselves, municipalities that had -- that did have more money, so that if a formation was operating in a municipality that had more money, was better paid, than a formation that was operating in a poorer municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the first few months after the conflicts began in that area, the area of the HZ HB, so we're talking about the period between April and June --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: July, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or August 1992, I don't think that anybody was financed at all. Nobody got any income, salaries, or anything for anything they did, be it work obligation, military obligation, or any other obligation or work. It was only when financial transaction system, payment system, was set up in that area that this issue was finally regulated. To my knowledge, all members of the Croatian Defence Council were paid, their salaries were quite low, but they did have those salaries. And those salaries were paid from the budget of the Croatian defence -- Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. So those were additional sources of financing for some of those units or formations; and it is likely that some municipalities were prepared to assist or to co-finance those formations, either because they thought that it would be easier to keep the security situation in that area under control or because they felt that they had enough money and that they could assist people who were involved in those units militarily.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, you answered my question at the very end. I would like to ask you to answer my questions directly because if you provide longer answers then you force me to ask ten follow-up questions. You say that all the formations were financed from the budget. Could you please tell me, if you know, whether the HVO up until the time that the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was established, whether it had any budget? Do you know that, did it have a budget?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it did and I think that the allocation of the funds in the budget was something that the finance department of the HZ HB dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, so I will not be dwelling on this because we will have an opportunity to look into that later. So you did tell me that some municipalities did finance those formations, that was your answer. Now I would like to ask you, Mr. Perkovic, could you please go back to the first document that I showed you, that is 1D 00296, that's dated the 26th of October, 1993, so up until that time this is what was happening, the additional funding from the municipalities. Let me ask you a hypothetical question, and I risk the objection of the Prosecution, but let me ask you this question nevertheless. Do you have any experience indicating that whoever is financing the troops has much more influence over the troops than other organs? Let me be quite specific. Does that mean that the municipal HVO could have influence, could exert greater influence, on the units operating in its area than, for instance, the Main Staff and other bodies that were involved in the defence of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, generally -- it is difficult to give a general answer to this question. For the best part it is limited by the power that the leader of the municipality exerted in any given municipality, and of course they -- their power was different in various areas. So my answer is that I cannot rule out the possibility that the municipal HVOs did exert influence over certain units and the possibility that this influence was greater than the influence exerted at the level of the department or other institutions of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you say, "I do not rule out," and my question is quite clear. Is it linked, or rather, does not the financing of those formations make it possible for such influence to be exerted? I'm not going to go municipality by municipality, although we can do that but it would take us a lot of time, but I'm sure you know how much influence was exerted by the presidents of the municipality in each and every municipality of the HZ HB. My question is: Does this financing give this kind of power?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's remark: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't doubt the fact that where there was more funding on the part of the municipality that the influence exerted over formations was greater. The more money you give, the more music you get. If you give somebody money you can ask for some favours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will now move on to a different topic -- is somebody saying something?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm being told that perhaps the time has come to our break -- well, I can see that Judge Trechsel is saying no, but at any rate I will be happy to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have ten minutes left before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at the document that comes next now, and that is 1D 01275. Today during the direct examination this document was referred to. Just tell me, Mr. Perkovic, when you find it. I'm briefly going to remind you what this is about. You were shown this document, and on page 23 of the transcript today from lines 9 to 16 you spoke about this, or rather, you answered questions about the function of the military council and how the military council was supposed to be appointed. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us be very specific. Your answer was rather accurate from the point of view of the regulations, and we are going to look at this particular regulation, but first of all I'm going to ask you whether this military council was established at all; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the establishment of a military council at any point in time. Today, as I was answering questions, I said what the powers of the military council were and who made up this military council according to the decree; however, I did not have any information to the effect that it was ever established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the next document in your binder and this is document number P 00588. The Prosecutors, the Judges, have a yellow sticker on this page; and I marked Article 18 so that the Judges and the Prosecutors wouldn't have to leaf through the entire document and you, Mr. Perkovic, in the Croatian version. So let us look at Article 18 together. Let us see how it reads so that we would be quite specific in relation to what it was that you said today. I can read it out: "A military council shall be established within the defence department as an advisory body, especially in matters of build-up, development, and supplies of the armed forces, but also in matters concerning the development of the defence doctrine and strategy of armed struggle. The military council shall consist of the head of the defence department and the Chief of the General Staff as well as of a certain number of members appointed by the HZ HB, president after consultations with the head of the defence department and Chief of General Staff." Mr. Perkovic, you said that as far as you know this military council was never established, that was your answer, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was that I did not know of this. I personally do not know whether it was ever established. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please have a look at the next document in the binder, it was established, and then we'll see if that will jog your memory. P 07090, that's the document. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was established only on the 19th [as interpreted] of December, 1993. The decision was signed by Mr. Boban, as it says in Article 18, the one that is invoked; and he invokes the reasons precisely in line with Article 18. It's already the defence ministry and that is the reference made in paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 the members of the Main Staff. Mr. Perkovic, can you remember now that this happened only in December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, this decision on the establishment of the military council is a document I see for the very first time now. I never had occasion to see this document, probably because by virtue of the work I performed at the time, I did not have access to documents of the president, especially not those that went through this line of publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Do not fear, nothing bad from me, just a correction of the transcript. It speaks in page 147, line 21, of the 19th September [sic] but I believe it's the 9th, at least in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just correct this, the decision on the establishment of the military council, as is written in document P 7090 is the 9th of December, the 9th of December, 1993. Thank you, Judge Trechsel. I'm not afraid of your interventions. I always consider them to be well-intentioned, so I look forward to interruptions on your part.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, you said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I must confess that this week I'm afraid that I may have -- I've overdone it a little but it was the interest of the material, but I'm aware that there may be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. All is well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you didn't know that the military council had been established, you did not attend these meetings; I understand that. But now I'm going to ask you about sessions of the HVO, whether there was any mention of the establishment of this military council and was it stated several times that the absence of this military council constituted a serious problem in the defence of the HZ HB. Do you remember that, this meeting included?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that at one or two sessions perhaps the issue was raised of the necessity of appointing, or rather, choosing or electing a military council. I think that at one of the HVO sessions Mr. Zubak spoke about that in the following way. He asked, or rather, re-initiated from that point of view the establishment of this military council. So I knew of this initiative. I knew what the military council did and who comprised it, but I did not know to this day, until a few moments ago, I never knew that it actually had been established, this military counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, the supreme council [as interpreted] without a military council, doesn't he have a lot more freedom and authority in decision-making if he does not have this kind of an advisory body, can one infer that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the role, or rather, the powers that the military council is supposed to have, obviously this is a body that is of an advisory nature, which is to say that suggestions or proposals of that body ultimately are not binding on the supreme commander, although by the very logic of things they can be of assistance and should be of assistance to the supreme council in terms of making the right kind of decisions, the best decisions, at a given point in time that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: An answer to this question would be logical. You rounded it off in a diplomatic way, but I'll ask you non-diplomatically. The fact that Mr. Mate Boban did not appoint a military council, doesn't it mean that in fact he didn't need one until December 1993, that even without any kind of advisory body he could make his own decisions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, Mr. Boban probably felt more comfortable without that kind of military council.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is very precious what you said, but I understood what you said by feeling more comfortable; but could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in our language the word "comfortable" is very clear. Now, what I wish to say is the following. To the extent to which I knew the president of the HZ HB, I think that he was a man who did not very much want to have institutions around him that would in a way meddle in the work that he considered to be his alone. In that context I believe that Mr. Boban was not really in a hurry to have this kind of council established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Perkovic, I have an intervention that on page 149, in line 15, it says supreme council and it should say supreme commander. Very well, now I would like to move on to another session, another topic that will require a bit more time. Are we going to take the break now or are we going to proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, I would like us to look at document 1D 01668. This document was shown to you today, precisely this part, that is to say the minutes of the 42nd Session of the HVO session on the 15th of June, 1993, and, as a matter of fact, part of this document was shown to you where the military security situation is discussed, Mr. Kvesic proposes what Mr. Stojic said and suggests and so on and so forth, not to go into all of it. For the transcript, there's no need to remind you, you remember that, that on pages 21, line 19, up to page 22, line 17 you explained how hard the situation was in Central Bosnia at the time. You did that very well, providing some details as well. Now I would like to ask you to look at the next two documents in the binder that precisely establish what it was that you said, and then we are going to go back to the conclusions from this session. Let us see what was going on in addition to what you had referred to. So could you please look at document 2D 00595. This is an operative report about the situation. It was submitted on the 8th of June, 1993, by the Croatian Defence Council, the command of the OZ, signed by Mr. Kostroman; the deputy prime minister, Mr. Ante Valenta; and then the vice-president, Mr. Kordic, they are all co-signatories; is that right, and it is signed by Mr. Tihomir Blaskic. Very briefly, I don't know whether you had an occasion to see this document early on?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not have an opportunity to do so because within my own line of work I did not receive operative reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read out some parts of the document for you so that you could confirm whether you remember these events. It says under number 1: "The situation at the defence lines is insignificant because an all-out attack has begun against all HVO positions, number of which positions, at the territory of the Lasva is getting smaller by the day and the ratio between HVO and ARBiH forces is 1:9 in favour of Muslims" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking me to do so. I will try.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: "I believe that an exodus has started from the Croats in Central Bosnia because there is no other choice, but to try to breakthrough towards Rama and Gornji Vakuf." Paragraph 2 is very dramatic saying: "We are aware that this is the last report that we are signing, we the most responsible individuals from a military and political point of view for the Croatian population in OZ Central Bosnia, population which is forced to flee the area where they live in front of the Muslim knife, even after more than 250 killed, slaughtered, many wounded, and a large number of disappeared civilians and soldiers." For the sake of speed I'm going to move on to paragraphs 4 and 5. 4 says: "We are going to begin destroying our documentation so if you have any further instructions please send them to us." And finally it says: "Please carry out all preparations for taking in expelled persons in an organized way." So this arrived a few days before the session, right? The HVO session where the situation in Central Bosnia was discussed? Have you -- had you heard about this situation and did you have information at that time that that is what the situation was in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to read this document or to be made aware of it at the time; but of course I did know about the disastrous situation where there was practically no way out, the situation in which the units and the Croatian population were in the so-called Lasva enclave, the Lasva river valley, that is, this is just one of the documents or segments showing how disastrous the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, and could you please look at the next document which is similar and it's an exhibit that is 2D 01407 which was submitted by Mr. Blaskic a day later on the 9th of June, 1993. It also speaks about the attack of the Muslim forces and the Mujahedin, the 7th Muslim Brigade, against this area. There is a reference to the attack against Guca Gora from the direction of Zenica about Croatian villages that were burned down and Croat civilians, women and children that were killed and harassed. It's an exhibit and it says at the very end: "We have consolidated our forces, the enemy has been repelled, Croatian soldiers understand that we can only defend ourselves using our own resources. Our basic objective and task is the defence of our areas. We shall persevere in this sacred and moral deed." Does this correspond to what you knew?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the document is somewhat different. This is a proclamation that was sent to all brigades of the armed forces of Central Bosnia HZ HB in that area. Obviously the intention was that it be made public in terms of portraying the situation realistically but also encouraging the population in the area, providing encouragement to the Croatian population in that area in Central Bosnia, or rather, the Lasva valley because radio stations like the radio of the HZ HB reported about the situation every day. So the citizens in the area who were listening - and I imagine most of them were - they were aware of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Perkovic, that was precisely my second question. From this proclamation, as you've called it, it is clear that the military command is doing its very best for the women and children, the civilians, and the army stay in that area rather than leave. Doesn't this document show that clearly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this document shows it clearly but only this -- not only this document but the fact that 250 people were killed in the fighting in an effort to keep those people there. This argument is much stronger than any other document -- any other argument against those who claim that some plans were made to move the population out, to evacuate them, and so on. I don't think that anyone in his right mind would allow 250 of his men to die, to be killed, yet at the same time to applaud the evacuation of that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see that my learned friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have an objection to the leading questions that have been asked in the last few questions. This evidence is beyond the scope of the evidence that this witness was supposed to be testifying to in the Rule 65 ter summary, so that will be direct examination rather than cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is pure cross-examination. I stressed the page of the transcript and my learned friend can check that. At page 21, line 19 through page 22 the witness spoke about the situation in Central Bosnia. I merely asked him whether these documents confirm what he had been telling us, nothing more than that, and I think this is cross-examination pure and simple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in this document we have a number of figures that come a bit as a surprise to me. Apparently 800 civilians were imprisoned in Guca Gora. Were you aware of that fact? And apparently 400 to 500 people were wounded, 500 missing, 400 people died. Don't you believe that Colonel Blaskic is exaggerating a bit when depicting the situation? I don't know for what purpose, but according to the information we have, these figures here do not quite reflect the situation as it was on the ground at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is really difficult for me to answer and provide specific figures for that time-period, but it is quite clear that the Croatian people in the Guca Gora local commune, which is part of the Travnik municipality, were at that time in a way cleansed from that area or moved out of that area, relocated. Now, whether there were 800 people or, I don't know, 750, 700 people, I really don't have those figures, so I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I would like to follow-up on what His Honour Judge Antonetti has just asked. A suggestion that I got, you said in your testimony that Travnik fell, that's what you said, so there's no need for us to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I would like to follow-up on what His Honour Judge Antonetti asked. I would just like to ask you if it is apparent from this that both of these memos reached first the president of the HZ HB and the second one to the chief of the Main Staff. The second memo reached the Main Staff and the defence department. Now, regardless of whether the number of victims is exaggerated, can we agree that this is the information that the HVO had immediately before this session that was supposed to discuss the military and security situation in this area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is just some of the information that the HVO HZ HB had when it considered this issue on the eve of this session. Other information reached the HVO regarding other areas and the situation was no better there, so this is just part of the information and the overall picture was quite bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a lot of documents that confirm what you've told us, but there will be other witnesses who may have been closer to that area and we will re-address this through them. Now I would like to ask you regarding the interventions by Mr. Stojic and others at the session. Can you confirm that that dramatic contents of their statements, does that -- does that correspond to what people from the HVO were saying, other people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about the 47th Session?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what was at the outset of that. Let me repeat, that is 1D 10668.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my firm belief that what Mr. Stojic said at this session was appropriate given the time and given the situation that prevailed in this area at that time. In his intervention at this session, Mr. Stojic is asking for the mobilisation, level of mobilisation, to be stepped-up in some municipalities, for a decision to withdraw military formations from some areas to be made, together with the Croatian population there. It is absolutely unrealistic to expect that you can withdraw any Croat soldier who would be ready to do so leaving his family, his wife, his children behind by retreating on his own. So this is fully consistent with the real situation. So if it was a political assessment that the military formations had to withdraw, it was impossible to do that if the people who were the cause why those soldiers took up arms were prohibited from leaving.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: His Honour Judge Antonetti asked you with regard to this document whether Mr. Prlic or anyone from the HVO could make any decisions that could interfere with the exercise of command in the army. I would like us to go back to this document to see what the conclusions are after this dramatic debate and whether these conclusions were in line with the powers that both the defence department and the HVO had at that time. So for the transcript let us go back to the document 1D 10668 to the conclusions which can be found at the end of the document. Number 1, you were at the session so this is an exhibit, there's no need for us to read it and to dwell on it for too long, but we can see that the situation is described in paragraph 1 of the conclusion; and it is stated at the end that: "In order to protect the population it is necessary -- a general mobilisation is urgently needed. In connection with this it is proposed to the supreme commander of the HVO, Mr. Mate Boban, to urgently meet with the Presidency of the HVO HZ HB, the Presidency of the HDZ, and the presidents of the municipal committees of the HDZ to organize the defence of all the Croatian areas which are under attack." Can you confirm then that this is fully within the remit of the HVO and the defence department as part of the HVO because this problem is sent up to the Presidency and the president and other organs that should deal with it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my opinion it is quite clear that in such a situation the HVO HZ HB would make the appropriate decisions in this sphere and that it had the powers to do so. It is quite clear from this that the Croatian Defence Council of the HZ HB did not have those powers. Those powers were vested in the institution of the president of the HZ HB and the president of the HDZ, and this is why the HVO puts together a proposal for possible measures in order for the competent authorities or institutions to take appropriate measures. The HVO assesses the dramatic situation. It does not have the power to take appropriate measures, but then suggests to the appropriate institution, which is the president of the HZ HB, to take appropriate measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You attended this session. Could you agree with me that all those conclusions, 1 through 7, were passed in accordance with the powers that the HVO had given the dramatic situation at the time? Could you please go through it quite quickly. I would not like us to dwell on this too long. I could go through this one by one, but let me give you some time to go through it but only if you can give me a generalised answer, not going into details one by one. Could you agree that these are the powers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the HVO in all those items, 1 through 7, did not deviate from the powers that it had.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the last document, that's 1D 01672. I read out the conclusions from the document 1D 10668, it's already been shown to the witness. I don't know if there is any confusion. So let me repeat, 1D 01688. So the last document that we mentioned is the minutes of the working meeting. Let me just check, when you were asked by His Honour Judge Antonetti, when he asked you about whether Mr. Stojic attended this meeting, we ascertained that he was and that in item 1 he spoke about the implementation of the decision to mobilise personnel. And in conclusions he was given certain tasks that pertained to this issue. I would just like us to ascertain that in item 1 in the minutes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down. The interpreters cannot find the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Slow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, a cry of distress from the interpreter's booth. They cannot follow, they do not find the clues. Maybe you start again a bit back because the last part wasn't translated anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I did not hear the cry of distress, but I have to say that now you scared me. Let me repeat what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So I will repeat everything to avoid any confusion. So these are the minutes from a working meeting of the HVO. The date is the 22nd of July, 1993, and in item 1, Mr. Stojic informed those present about the implementation of the decision on mobilisation of troops, that's at page 1 -- I think it's not difficult to find it. And then in conclusions we can see that he was given some tasks. And now I would like you -- to ask, if you look at the agenda at item 1, can we conclude that Mr. Stojic first provides information about what is within the purview of the defence department; and second, that he was bound to provide this kind of information on the 17th of July, 1993, that he was given this task?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have said this and let me repeat this again, that I could not remember who was present at the meeting, so I couldn't recall whether Mr. Stojic was there. As regards what you're asking me, I can just give you an answer based on what I have in front of me. It is quite clear that the issue of mobilisation is within the purview of the defence department of the HVO HZ HB. In this context Mr. Stojic spoke about something that is in essence his job, and he informed all those present about the success rate of the mobilisation in the area of the HZ HB. Since I don't have the conclusions from the working meeting of the 17th of July, 1993, I can only assume that in one of those conclusions Mr. Stojic was given a task to inform the HVO about the progress of the mobilisation in a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what follows from the document. In the end, let me ask you just two brief questions about the Commission For Regulations that you were in the HZ HB. First question: Did you -- did the commission have the power when a certain draft law reached it to ascertain whether it is in line with the other laws enacted by the HZ HB and whether this law would be in contravention of other legislation, would you then return the law back to the sender?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, your job in the Commission For Regulations, which was then superseded by the legislation office during the existence of the HR HB was precisely this, to assess the level of harmonization of various pieces of legislation. To make things simpler, we were there to prevent a situation where one decree would deal with an issue in one way and the -- another decree would stipulate something else, and then you would have this collision, this conflict. So it was our job to prevent the collision of different provisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, if you were to receive a document to review and if it were against international standards, or rather, say not in line with the Geneva Conventions specifically, would you return it and would you say that it was in contravention of an international standard or document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN PERKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we would do that. When I first testified before this Tribunal, when answering a question I said - and I stand by that today as well - namely, that I state with full responsibility that in the entire legal system of the HZ HB and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna there is not a single regulation or norm that is discriminatory and that treats any citizen from the area in any different way during that period of time, irrespective of ethnicity or any other affiliation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Perkovic. We have already heard that. I was just interested in the first part of your answer. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would, if I may, I would like to ask for a clarification. On page 160, lines 21, 22, 23, you are written down as having said: "It is quite clear that the issue of mobilisation is within the purview of the defence department of the HVO HZ HB." In the decree on the armed forces in Article 9, number 6, it says: "The Croatian Defence Council shall decide on conducting mobilisation ..." This at first glance seems to be a contradiction. I'm sure you can clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Croatian Defence Council and in accordance with that decree makes a decision on the implementation of mobilisation; however, the question of the implementation of that decision, that is to say the immediate implementation of that decision in the field, in reality, is within the purview of the defence department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I noticed, if I may intervene, I have observed this answer, but I believe that we have clarified that fully today, what the HVO and what the defence department are supposed to do. And since we have the decree on armed forces before us, I think it would be very important to look at Article 37, which says that it is the president of the HZ HB that orders mobilisation. So as far as mobilisation is concerned, there are different stages involved and preparations in terms of the regulations involved, the defence department included. That is how I understood Mr. Perkovic's answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to move to another level. Based on the last two documents submitted to you by Ms. Nozica, that is, the 9th of June document by Tihomir Blaskic as to the situation in Central Bosnia and the 22nd of July meeting in which Mr. Stojic under item 1 mention the issue of mobilisation. If you look closely at these two documents, in June and July 1993 the situation seems to be very worrying militarily speaking because there was an offensive by the ABiH and if we are to believe Mr. Blaskic, who may have exaggerated the figures, but there is concrete evidence, 39 villages seem to have been occupied and devastated, 225.000 Croats risk being refugees, there's a high number of people that were killed, wounded, or missing. In Mr. Blaskic's document there is a small detail that seems absolutely essential to me. He writes that the ratio of the forces in presence would be 1:10, so one Croatian soldier for ten ABiH soldiers. We know that the 3rd Corps of the ABiH had more than 100.000 soldiers, so these are very impressive figures. In military terms one question is obvious: How can you face a situation such as this whilst you have less people to the extent of a ratio of 1:10? Apparently the answer given by the authorities of Herceg-Bosna is to mobilise. Very well. There could be a mobilisation, but this would entail that you basically have to mobilise a high ratio of people since there is basically ten times as many ABiH soldiers as HVO soldiers. Based on this situation which is abundantly described during HVO meetings in which you participated, I'm allowed to conclude that there is a real military problem; but it is also a political one, namely, is the policy that has been adopted and implemented the right one and should there not be another type of policy? But the documents we've seen do not demonstrate any discussion whatsoever among heads of municipalities, among leaders, or with Mr. Prlic. If there was no discussion at HVO level, I mean the civilian HVO, in your view where did political discussions take place? Was it discussed in Mr. Boban's office? Faced with such a situation, was he forced to position himself politically? That's the source for my surprise. When I look at these documents, I note that military situation is extremely worrying and the only answer provided is to mobilise. Was it enough though? Where can we find traces of political discussions? They're not to be found anywhere, so could it be that there were other discussions that we can't see anywhere? You participated in the meetings, so what do you think of it? What do you have to say? Sorry for the length of my question, but I had to sum up the situation based on the documents. In order to put the questions to you I can't just sort of put a brief question to you. I have to give you all the ins and outs, as it were, in order for you to answer properly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question of mobilisation in certain areas is not the only response and cannot be the only response to such a situation. I'm not a soldier, but I assume that this mobilisation was aimed at additionally reducing the pressure that was at the ratio that you refer to, 1:10, in that area. As far as political decisions are concerned, throughout the existence of the Croatian Community and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna they were related to the negotiating process of seeking peace or trying to find a peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina. As for the conduct of these negotiations and participation in these negotiations, it was the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna who carried this out. So the institution of the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, if I can put it this way, included political prerogatives of reaching political decisions that in this or that way were expressed through different peace programmes in which, or rather, in whose preparation the representatives of the Croatian people from Bosnia-Herzegovina took part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your answer. We have a few minutes left before we adjourn. The Prosecutor could, in theory, start with the cross-examination, but you might want to start tomorrow. Is it going to be Mr. Stringer or Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will do the cross-examination, but I agree with your proposal to start tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we've got eight minutes left. I shall use the time to tell the witness that he will have to return. Tomorrow we'll start at 9.00 -- oh, tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning, yes, that's tomorrow because I have a hearing at 2.15 so I can't be wrong. Tomorrow morning -- is that right, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct, we are meeting at 9.00 tomorrow morning -- I guess we are -- right? I was going to be asking if we could get -- I know the Prosecution doesn't wish to have the witness look at the documents, I guess maybe they fear that he may come up with some answers and prepare them overnight, but at least can the lawyers get ahold of the Prosecution documents since we are not going to be contacting the witness, we haven't done that, we don't intend to do that; but I do like to prepare and be vigilant, if necessary, in order to properly phrase my objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, since Mr. Karnavas put it in such a way in front of the witness I'll respond in a likewise way. No, the Prosecution doesn't agree to disclose the binders to the Defence because they never disclosed the binders to us when our witnesses were being called. So we're going to stick very precisely to the same procedure that applied when the Defence was cross-examining Prosecution witnesses. So that's just how the game has been played, if you will, and that's how we propose to continue to play the game. The witness is aware, no witness sees any of the documents for cross until he begins his testimony. That's how it's been virtually through the entire trial and that's how it's going to be for Mr. Perkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we're not asking for the witness to see the documents - and I don't see this as a game and I know this is just an expression - I was wondering if the lawyers, if I could see the documents now. I don't see what the harm is. Of course, if they think that perhaps I might be overly prepared by tomorrow, somehow I may confuse the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that Mr. Stringer has answered already, but he say want to add something. Does that position apply to everybody, including the Judges, because I don't have the documents either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, I remember very well during our part of the case counsel walking across and giving us the documents at the moment they begin their cross-examination, and that's why we're going to adhere to the very same procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I would want to press this issue. Now, I do think -- okay, I'm not going to get the documents, that's fine. I think I can manage, I think I can manage, but to deny the Bench, I think that's an affront to the Judges. The Judges should be entitled to have the documents. God forbid that the Judges be prepared to ask questions, as they're entitled to. So I'm a little shocked to hear this and certainly he may wish to reconsider.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I didn't understand that the Bench was requesting them. Clearly, if the Bench is requesting the documents, we'll provide them, we'll provide them to the Bench at any time, but I'm addressing my remarks to those by Mr. Karnavas. He knows the procedures that they were all too willing to use during the Prosecution case, and that's how it's going to be now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, none of Your Honours require me, least of all, to come to the defence of the Bench, so I don't address that particular point. But I would, with the greatest of respect and humility deprecate, and I know it wasn't meant by my learned friend, the misuse of the analogy of this being a game. There is a distinction, of course. The Prosecution have said repeatedly, at least twice I remember, that they're representing the international community and they are also representing the victims. And the principles of transparency and cause in a tabled approach would militate, in my respectful submission, all things being equal, to documents which they're putting to a witness being given to their professional colleagues. Now, of course it may be, it may be, that the Defence don't have the moral high ground if they didn't extend this courtesy to the Prosecution in similar circumstances. I won't speak to that. I came late into this case. But that doesn't affect, in my respectful submission, the overriding obligation of the Prosecution - and my learned friend knows his duties and responsibilities most vividly - to ensure that they conduct prosecutions to the highest ethical standards. And I don't see for the life of me how the Prosecution being the voice of the international community in this courtroom supposedly would be prejudiced by giving documents, which presumably have been disclosed in advance to the parties, to professional colleagues and to the Bench in advance of cross-examining a witness. To me, it seems rather spiteful and mean. As I said, it may be that the Defence have -- are in some difficult position because they behaved in a certain manner, I don't know. Your Honour, I don't speak to that issue, but I do see in my submission the position being rather untenable and rather unfortunate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It so happens that during the Prosecution case the Prosecution did ask the Defence to receive the documents the Defence had intended to use during cross-examination, I remember that, but you were not in the case yet, Mr. Khan. The Defence refused that and they said that the Prosecution would get the document just before the cross-examination, so under the principle of equality of arms the same should apply now. As to the Judges, in theory of course the Judges can be given documents, but you must have understood that already; we are perfectly able to use a document straight away, as soon as we discover it. So technically speaking, I don't need to have the documents hours in advance. You can give it to me now and five seconds later I can ask a question. So personally, personally, I do not feel the need to have documents ahead of time. So we're all going to be very calm and collected and wait tomorrow until 9.00, then we'll have the little tray with all the binders. This being said, I wish you a good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of September, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
